quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In standard musical notation, what do the two numbers in a 3/4 time signature tell a performer about the meter of the piece?
quiz_item.question: In standard musical notation, what do the two numbers in a 3/4 time signature tell a performer about the meter of the piece?
options: A. Play three measures per line at a tempo of four beats per second.
B. Divide the ensemble into three vocal parts and raise the pitch by four half-steps.
C. There are three beats in each measure, and a quarter note receives one full beat.
D. There are four beats in each measure, and a dotted half note receives three beats.
choices: A. Play three measures per line at a tempo of four beats per second.
B. Divide the ensemble into three vocal parts and raise the pitch by four half-steps.
C. There are three beats in each measure, and a quarter note receives one full beat.
D. There are four beats in each measure, and a dotted half note receives three beats.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. There are three beats in each measure, and a quarter note receives one full beat.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): In a time signature, the top number indicates how many beats are in each measure (three), while the bottom number indicates which note value receives one beat (4 stands for a quarter note).

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Attend a live performance, or listen to three hours of recordings from any two of the following musical styles: blues, jazz, classical, country, bluegrass, ethnic, gospel, musical theater, opera. Describe the sound of the music and the instruments used. Identify the composers or songwriters, the performers, and the titles of the pieces you heard. If it was a live performance, describe the setting and the reaction of the audience. Discuss your thoughts about the music. (b) Interview an adult member of your family about music. Find out what the most popular music was when he or she was your age. Find out what his or her favorite music is now, and listen to three of your relative's favorite tunes with him or her. How do those favorites sound to you? Had you ever heard any of them? Play three of your favorite songs for your relative, and explain why you like these songs. Ask what he or she thinks of your favorite music. (c) Serve for six months as a member of a school band, choir, or other organized musical group, or perform as a soloist in public six times. (d) List five people who are important in the history of American music and explain to your counselor why they continue to be influential. Include at least one composer, one performer, one innovator, and one person born more than 100 years ago.

requirements.description: Do TWO of the following: (a) Attend a live performance, or listen to three hours of recordings from any two of the following musical styles: blues, jazz, classical, country, bluegrass, ethnic, gospel, musical theater, opera. Describe the sound of the music and the instruments used. Identify the composers or songwriters, the performers, and the titles of the pieces you heard. If it was a live performance, describe the setting and the reaction of the audience. Discuss your thoughts about the music. (b) Interview an adult member of your family about music. Find out what the most popular music was when he or she was your age. Find out what his or her favorite music is now, and listen to three of your relative's favorite tunes with him or her. How do those favorites sound to you? Had you ever heard any of them? Play three of your favorite songs for your relative, and explain why you like these songs. Ask what he or she thinks of your favorite music. (c) Serve for six months as a member of a school band, choir, or other organized musical group, or perform as a soloist in public six times. (d) List five people who are important in the history of American music and explain to your counselor why they continue to be influential. Include at least one composer, one performer, one innovator, and one person born more than 100 years ago.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

requirements.description: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In standard musical notation, what do the two numbers in a 3/4 time signature tell a performer about the meter of the piece?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In standard musical notation, what do the two numbers in a 3/4 time signature tell a performer about the meter of the piece?
options: A. Play three measures per line at a tempo of four beats per second.
B. Divide the ensemble into three vocal parts and raise the pitch by four half-steps.
C. There are three beats in each measure, and a quarter note receives one full beat.
D. There are four beats in each measure, and a dotted half note receives three beats.
choices: A. Play three measures per line at a tempo of four beats per second.
B. Divide the ensemble into three vocal parts and raise the pitch by four half-steps.
C. There are three beats in each measure, and a quarter note receives one full beat.
D. There are four beats in each measure, and a dotted half note receives three beats.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. There are three beats in each measure, and a quarter note receives one full beat.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): In a time signature, the top number indicates how many beats are in each measure (three), while the bottom number indicates which note value receives one beat (4 stands for a quarter note).
